Re-measured on the rebase of this branch onto origin/19.0-marin, not carried across as arithmetic.

This branch banked 358 -> 356 for website's _compute_first_page_id and stock_delivery's
_compute_allowed_carrier_ids (both still fixed, both still pinned by their batch-cost
tests). origin had independently re-measured 359 after banking event's two batched loops.
Neither number survives the merge: the rebased tree reads 355 under the CI command,
`tooling/lint/py_lint.py odoo addons --count`, n-plus-one-query row.

An exact floor fails downward as well as up, so the floor is the measurement rather than
either side's delta added to the other's base -- 356 and 359 would each have failed every
PR until someone re-measured.

--- APPENDED ON REBASE, 2026-08-29: 355 -> 352.

origin measures 355 and banked 355; this branch takes odoo/orm to zero on the rule (_convert_records' one-search-per-imported-row, plus the documented waiver on one2many.write_real's CLEAR/SET branch), for -3.

352 is a fresh measurement of the rebased tree with this gate's own --count, not arithmetic on the two notes. The superseded note from this branch follows.

--- SUPERSEDED NOTE FROM THIS BRANCH:

website, stock_delivery: two more per-record loops. ir.ui.view._compute_first_page_id ran website.page.search(limit=1) once per view, which is a query per row of the Website > Pages list -- 21 queries for 20 views, now 2, pinned by TestFirstPageIdBatchCost. stock.picking._compute_allowed_carrier_ids searched delivery.carrier per picking when the domain only varies by company; the batch pass now resolves it per company, 20 queries for 6 pickings -> 15, 48 for 20 -> 29. That one does not go flat and this is not the reason: the ORM calls the compute for the whole recordset and then again once per record, on the original code as well.

Banked from a measurement of the rebased tree, not from arithmetic. Before the rebase this branch read 358 -> 356; origin had independently re-measured 359 after banking event's two batched loops. An exact floor fails downward as well as up, so the merged count is the one the CI command reports -- `tooling/lint/py_lint.py odoo addons --count`, n-plus-one-query row -- rather than either side's delta carried across.

--- APPENDED ON REBASE, 2026-08-29: 356 -> 352. TWO DISJOINT REPAIRS, AND A
FLOOR THAT WAS ONE ABOVE ITS OWN TREE.

Three figures, each a separate `tooling/lint/py_lint.py odoo addons --count` run
reading the n-plus-one-query row, none of them arithmetic:

    355   origin/19.0-marin at 50cc6023974, against a banked 356 -- the floor
          sat one above the tree it was banked on, so an exact ratchet was
          failing the FALLING way for everyone before this branch touched it
    352   that tree with this branch replayed onto it
    ---
     -3   this branch's actual contribution

The two repairs are disjoint and therefore compose, which is the property this
gate has and mypy's floor does not: origin batched ir.ui.view._compute_first_page_id
and stock.picking._compute_allowed_carrier_ids (the note above), while this branch
took odoo/orm to zero on the rule -- _convert_records' one-search-per-imported-row,
plus the documented waiver on one2many.write_real's CLEAR/SET branch. Both notes
are kept because both bodies of work are in the tree; only the endpoints they
each quote (359 -> 356 and 358 -> 356) describe trees that no longer exist.

--- SUPERSEDED NOTE FROM THIS BRANCH, KEPT FOR THE REASONING:

358 -> 356: odoo/orm reaches zero on this rule, one waived and one fixed.

The waiver is one2many.write_real's CLEAR/SET branch, where the search runs
immediately after a flush() that has just moved rows -- each iteration
deliberately observes a different database, so there is nothing to hoist.

The fix is _convert_records, which ran ONE SEARCH PER IMPORTED ROW carrying a
.id. It now resolves every .id in a single search before the loop. Nothing was
streaming that this materialises: load() drains the generator into a list before
doing anything with it. Same query count for well-formed input. A non-numeric
.id used to reach search([('id','=','abc')]), which _optimize_numeric_comparand
answers with an empty Domain, and is now simply not in the resolved set -- the
same 'Unknown database identifier' message, one query earlier.

Measured -i test_lint at CI scope in a detached worktree at c0a918326d3: 358
with nothing applied, 356 with only this change's odoo/orm files copied in.
